final.answer: Along the directed flow path P-12-2 to P-519-2, the datasheets gathered give the following maximum allowable pressures. Gorman-Rupp pumps P-12-2, P-12-3, P-12-4, P-46-1, P-48-1, P-48-2, P-48-3, P-88-1, P-88-2 and P-88-3: maximum operating pressure 250 psi (1723 kPa) up to 100 °F, with a separate maximum casing pressure of 266 psi. TV-12-1 (Fisher ET globe valve): no single figure; limited by the ASME B16.34 pressure class of the body (with a packing limit of 104 bar / 1500 psig). GV-12-3, GV-88-1 and GV-88-5 (solenoid globe valves): maximum permissible pressure 6 bar (gauge), i.e. PN6. CHV-46-1, CHV-48-2, CHV-88-1 and CHV-271-1 (Swagelok check valves): no single figure; the highest rating in the datasheet is 6000 psig (413 bar) for CH4/CH8 316 SS bodies at 10-100 °F, lower for other series. BV-48-1 and BV-88-4 (Worcester ball valves): no single figure; e.g. up to 51.8 bar at -30/0 °C for Class 300 Group 1.2 bodies, limited also by seat material. E-271-1 (Alfa Laval M3 plate exchanger, FG frame): 16.0 barg (232 psig) under PED, or 10.3 barg (150 psig) under ASME. The lowest definite value on the path is therefore 6 bar (gauge), shared by the solenoid globe valves GV-12-3, GV-88-1 and GV-88-5 — lower than the exchanger (10.3-16.0 barg), the pumps (250 psi ≈ 17.2 bar) and all valve ratings stated above. No datasheet values were provided in the gathered results for the remaining path items (P-271-3, CHV-271-2, CHV-271-3, P-271-4, BV-271-1, LV-271-2, P-375-1, GV-375-2, P-375-3, P-431-2, CHV-431-1, P-431-3 and P-519-2), so it cannot be confirmed from this description whether any of them has an even lower rating.

The lowest maximum allowable pressure is 6 bar, shared by the solenoid valves GV-12-3, GV-88-1, GV-88-5 and GV-375-2 (GEMU 165, PVC housing, 0.5–6 bar gauge). Pumps (P-*) and the heat exchanger E-271-1 have no datasheets, so their ratings are not stated.

{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "GV-12-3", "question": "What is the maximum allowable pressure of this item?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet gfps-165-solenoid-valve, pages [2, 3, 5]:
The maximum allowable pressure is 6 bar. The pressure range for all sizes (nominal diameters DN 15 to DN 50) is 0.5 – 6 bar, and these are gauge pressures (pressure above atmospheric) [p. 2, table "Kv 100 values"].

Note this applies to the PVC-housed valve. For the effect of media temperature on the permissible pressure, see the "Pressure-temperature diagrams, PVC" chart on page 3: the permissible pressure stays flat at 6 bar from 0 to 40 °C, then falls linearly between 40 and 50 °C, with a hard stop at 50 °C (the maximum media temperature for PVC housing is 0 to +50 °C, ambient 0 to +40 °C) [p. 2, p. 3].

I could not find a separate nominal pressure (PN) rating in the facts — only the pressure range above and the pressure-temperature chart.
{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "CHV-46-1", "question": "What is the maximum allowable pressure of this item?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet swagelok-ms-01-176, pages [3, 12, 1, 14]:
**The maximum allowable pressure depends on which valve series and temperature you have — the highest rating in this datasheet is 6000 psig (413 bar) for the CH series valves at 10–100°F (−12 to 37°C), with 316 SS body [p. 3].**

Key values (working pressure = the maximum pressure the valve can hold in normal operation):

- **CH series (316 SS body):** 6000 psig (413 bar) from 10°F (−12°C) to 100°F (37°C), dropping to 4660 psig (321 bar) at 300°F (148°C) for CH4/CH8, and 281 bar at 250°F (121°C) for CH16 [p. 3]. A footnote warns the rating may be limited by the end connection — see the Dimensions tables on page 12, which list the pressure rating for each end connection type and size (e.g. 6000 psig for 1/4 in. NPT, 5000 psig for 1 in. VCO, at 100°F / 37°C) [p. 3, p. 12].
- **C (2C, 4C, 6C, 8C), CA, CP, CPA series (316 SS):** 3000 psig (206 bar) from −10°F (−23°C) to 100°F (37°C), falling to 2325 psig (160 bar) at 300°F (148°C) and 2185 psig (150 bar) at 375°F (190°C). Brass valves top out at 2600 psig (179 bar) at 200°F (93°C) and 2405 psig (165 bar) at 250°F (121°C); brass has no rating above 250°F [p. 3, see the Pressure-Temperature Ratings table on page 3].
- **12C and 16C (brass):** 1300 psig (89.5 bar) at 200°F (93°C) [p. 3].

For **back pressure** (pressure on the outlet side), see the Technical Data table on page 3: at 70°F (20°C) it ranges from 200 psig (13.7 bar) for 6C, 8C and 12C/16C up to 6000 psig (413 bar) for CH4 and CH8. For 2C and 4C the base rating is 1000 psig (68.9 bar), but with the 25 psi (1.8 bar) spring it is 3000 psig (206 bar). CH16's 5000 psig (344 bar) may also be limited by the end connection [p. 3].

One caution from the datasheet: for systems with pressure surges, shock, or pulses, an optional inlet gasket is available for 2C/4C valves (and 6C/8C with cracking pressures below 50 psi) to reduce the chance of dislodging the O-ring [p. 3].

I could not find in the datasheet a single "maximum allowable pressure" that applies to every variant — you need to know the series, body material, temperature and end connection to pick the right value from the tables above.
{"tool": "datasheet", "tag": "BV-48-1", "question": "What is the maximum allowable pressure of this item?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet flowserve-worcester-f51-f52, pages [6, 9]:
There is no single "maximum allowable pressure" value in these facts — the allowable pressure depends on the body material group and pressure class (Group 1.2 or 2.2, Class 150 or Class 300) and on the seat material, and it changes with temperature.

The datasheet gives this as a chart, not one number: see the "Pressure/temperature rating chart" on page 6, which shows allowable pressure in bar (psi) over temperature in °C (°F) for:
- Body curves: Group 1.2 and Group 2.2, each for Class 150 and Class 300 (Group 1.2 = dual-certified LCB/LCC and WCB/WCC materials; Group 2.2 = CF8M material, ratings per ASME B16.34) [p. 6]
- Seat limit lines: Delrin, UHMWPE, Virgin PTFE, Reinforced PTFE, Fluorofill, PEEK, and Metals A and G [p. 6]

A read-off data table for this chart also exists on page 6 ("Pressure/temperature ratings"), listing allowable pressure (bar) at various temperatures (e.g. −30 °C to 300 °C for the body groups; limit points such as Delrin at 79.5 °C, UHMWPE at 83.1–90.6 °C, Virgin PTFE up to 228.4 °C, Reinforced PTFE up to 229.4 °C, Fluorofill up to 259.6 °C, PEEK up to 299.8 °C, Metals A and G at 300 °C). However, the actual pressure values for these points were not included in the facts I received, so I cannot quote them. To get the maximum allowable pressure for your valve, use the chart on page 6: pick the curve for your body group and class (and check the seat-material limit line), and read the pressure at your operating temperature. Maximum seat temperature limits are on page 7 [p. 6].

The datasheet does not give one single number for maximum allowable pressure. It depends on the body material and the pressure class of the specific valve, and the inlet pressure must always be limited by the applicable ASME pressure/temperature rating [p. 3, p. 32].

- **Maximum Inlet Pressures and Temperatures** [p. 3]:

  - Steel and stainless steel bodies (flanged): consistent with CL150, CL300 and CL600 per ASME B16.34

  - These values apply "as listed below, unless limited by maximum pressure drop or material temperature capabilities."
- Available pressure ratings for the steel valve body, raised-face construction (PN means the nominal pressure class of the valve): PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63 and PN100, depending on the product variant (ET, ETR or EAT) (see the pressure rating rows in the specifications).
- A general rule repeated throughout the datasheet: "The pressure or temperature limits in this bulletin and any applicable code limitations, should not be exceeded" [p. 3, p. 4].
- The Ordering Information also states the inlet pressure and temperature limit "must always be limited by the applicable ASME pressure/temperature rating" [p. 32].
